newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten an optimist about Hong Kong's future - report.
newsitem.headline: Patten an optimist about Hong Kong's future - report.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said he was optimistic about Hong Kong's prospects after it reverted to China's rule, although much would depend on Beijing.
"I am, on balance, an optimist about Hong Kong. It has managed over the years to cope with some pretty hairy situations," Patten told Time magazine in an edition seen in Asia on Monday.
"If people are given a bit of elbowroom, if China relaxes about Hong Kong, I think that everything will be fine. Of course, a huge amount depends on what happens in China itself," he said.

He defended electoral reforms he introduced to the territory that resulted in greater democracy in legislative polls but angered China, which retakes the British colony of 156 years at midnight on June 30.

"What would have been the advantage for Hong Kong if I hadn't changed our (electoral) laws to bring them in line with the Bill of Rights? We would have just had fewer freedoms before 1997 -- with Britain's chop on it," he said.
"As it is, people in Hong Kong now have a few benchmarks. They know what a free election is like," he said.
"I don't think I brought democracy," he said. "I responded to the pressures of an increasingly well-educated, prosperous, well-travelled community."
Patten said Britain could take some credit for the achievements of Hong Kong, which has expanded from a small fishing port into an international financial centre.
"The Hong Kong that Britain leaves on June 30 is one of the greatest cities in the world. I think we can take a smidgen of credit," he said.
